assessment.summary: KRAS is one of the most extensively studied oncology targets with exceptional structural, chemical, and literature evidence. Two approved covalent inhibitors (sotorasib and adagrasib) targeting the G12C mutation validate the target clinically, and the deep chemical matter (>5900 IC50 entries) and 556 PDB structures reflect decades of intensive drug discovery efforts. Druggability is high for G12C-mutant KRAS specifically, with ongoing work expanding coverage to other oncogenic variants.
evidence_gaps: Approved drugs (sotorasib, adagrasib) are selective for the G12C mutation only; druggability of other common mutants (G12D, G12V, G13D) and wild-type KRAS remains less established clinically, though tool compounds exist
Median IC50 of ~1020 nM across all ChEMBL entries reflects historical difficulty in achieving potent non-covalent inhibition; potency profile for non-G12C inhibitors is generally weaker

Resistance mechanisms (e.g., secondary mutations, bypass signalling via RTKs, RAS amplification) are well-documented and may limit durable clinical benefit, but are not captured in static druggability metrics
Allele-specific or pan-RAS inhibitor strategies are still in early clinical/preclinical stages with no approved agents beyond G12C
Combination strategies needed for most KRAS-driven tumours are not reflected in single-target druggability scores
